text:
Mark Scheifele now stands alone as the Jets' all-time points leader, and he got there in the most Winnipeg way possible this season: four points and a shootout goal as the Jets erased a four-goal deficit in Chicago and won 5-4. As the Winnipeg Free Press's Ken Wiebe noted, it was another four-goal comeback. This team refuses to stay down.

It's a different Jets team than the one people expected. Connor Hellebuyck forced his way to New Jersey, Stuart Skinner is the goalie now, and Dawson Mercer has fit in quickly with his new team, eight points in his last ten games, including two goals in an 8-3 win in Dallas. Winnipeg has won six straight, outscoring teams 32-18, with 59% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in those games.

The season-long numbers are more modest. At 10-8-3 with 23 points, the Jets have taken 48% of the five-on-five expected goals, and our playoff odds sit at 36%. The power play is a weapon at 0.84 expected goals a game, but the penalty kill gives nearly as much back.

Scheifele and Kyle Connor are the engine, with Cole Perfetti on their line outscoring teams 9-6. Dylan Samberg and Neal Pionk carry the blue line. What we'd watch: whether the streak's process holds when the comebacks stop being necessary, and how Skinner handles the workload.
